questions.prompt: 9-handed, 100bb, folded to the button with KJo. Best default?

choices.text: Fold. Offsuit broadways are never opened.
Limp. The button should never raise.
All-in. Late position means stack off.

questions.explanation: KJo is a standard button open and a poor under-the-gun open.

questions.prompt: 6-handed, folded to the earliest seat with ATo at 100bb. Compared with 9-handed UTG, you should…

choices.text: Open. This seat is much later than a full-ring UTG.
Fold. The first seat is always a 9-handed UTG range.

questions.explanation: Six-handed early position is closer to a full-ring hijack or cutoff.

questions.prompt: Folded to the cutoff with 72o at a 9-handed table. What do you do?

choices.text: Open. Any two cards are a cutoff open.
Fold. 72o is still too weak with the button and blinds behind.

questions.explanation: The cutoff opens wide, not randomly. 72o is a fold until the game is extremely short-handed.

questions.prompt: Button, 100bb, folded to you with 22. A reasonable plan is…

choices.text: Fold. Pairs cannot be opened in late position.
Limp and fold to a min-raise.
Open, and fold to a large 3-bet from a tight blind.

questions.explanation: Small pairs open on the button for set value and position, then release versus a strong reraise.
